record.context_brief: Bregman analogues of Chebyshev and Klee functions
record.original_question: In the theory of Chebyshev functions and Klee functions for a proper lower semicontinuous function g: X -> [-infinity, +infinity], the paper uses the halved Euclidean distance q = (1/2)||.||^2 through the proximal map P_lambda g and the farthest map Q_mu g. What are the corresponding characterizations when the Euclidean discrepancy is replaced by a Bregman distance generated by a Legendre function f? In particular, how should one characterize the admissible generator f and the analogue of the Chebyshev point in that Bregman setting?

evidence.quote: Chebyshev set and Klee set problems can be generalized to problems involving functions. Throughout this section, g : X -> [-infinity, +infinity] is lower semicontinuous and proper.
For convenience, we also set q := 1/2 ||.||^2.
Problem 7. For the Chebyshev functions and Klee functions, we have used the halved Euclidean distance. What are characterizations of f and Chebyshev point of f when one uses the Bregman distances?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Euclidean space, and let $g:X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$ be a proper lower semicontinuous function. For a parameter $\lambda>0$, the proximal map and farthest map of $g$ relative to the halved squared Euclidean distance $q(\cdot)=\tfrac12\|\cdot\|^2$ are
$$P_\lambda g(x)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{y\in X}\Big(g(y)+\tfrac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-y\|^2\Big),\qquad Q_\mu g(x)=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{y\in X}\Big(g(y)-\tfrac{1}{2\mu}\|x-y\|^2\Big).$$
The function $g$ is called a Chebyshev function (resp. Klee function) when $P_\lambda g$ (resp. $Q_\mu g$) is single-valued on its natural domain. A point realizing the unique minimizer (resp. maximizer) is called the Chebyshev point of $g$ at $x$.

Now replace the squared Euclidean discrepancy by a Bregman distance. Let $f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a Legendre function in the sense of Rockafellar (i.e., $f$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, essentially smooth, and essentially strictly convex), with $\operatorname{int\,dom}f\neq\emptyset$. The associated Bregman distance is
$$D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-\langle \nabla f(y),x-y\rangle,\qquad x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ y\in\operatorname{int\,dom}f.$$
Define accordingly the Bregman proximal and farthest maps of $g$ by
$$P^f_\lambda g(x)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{y}\big(g(y)+\tfrac{1}{\lambda}D_f(y,x)\big),\qquad Q^f_\mu g(x)=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{y}\big(g(y)-\tfrac{1}{\mu}D_f(y,x)\big),$$
(or with the arguments of $D_f$ reversed, giving the right Bregman variant).

Problem. Provide characterizations, in this Bregman setting, of:
(i) the Legendre generators $f$ for which the Bregman analogues of Chebyshev functions and Klee functions admit a clean theory paralleling the Euclidean case (in particular, conditions on $f$ ensuring uniqueness of the Bregman proximal/farthest minimizer for suitable classes of $g$);
(ii) the Bregman Chebyshev point of $f$, i.e., a usable description of the unique optimizer in (i) and of when a proper lower semicontinuous $g$ qualifies as a Bregman Chebyshev function or Bregman Klee function.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed important parts of this question: results of Bauschke–Macklem–Wang and others establish that Klee sets with respect to right Bregman distances induced by Legendre functions are singletons under suitable hypotheses, and provide uniqueness of Chebyshev centers. Studies of Legendre functions whose gradients map convex sets to convex sets, and of Klee/Chebyshev problems for Bregman distances in Banach space settings, give partial structural characterizations of admissible generators. However, a complete characterization of the admissible Legendre generator $f$ and a fully general description of the Bregman Chebyshev point for arbitrary proper lsc $g$ does not appear to have been settled.

status_evidence.title: Klee sets and Chebyshev centers for the right Bregman distance
status_evidence.snippet: Affirmative answer that every Klee set with respect to the right Bregman distance is a singleton, with uniqueness of the Chebyshev center.
status_evidence.claim: Partial resolution of the Klee/Chebyshev question in the Bregman setting.

status_evidence.title: Bregman distances and Klee sets in Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Extends Klee-set/Chebyshev-center results to Bregman distances in Banach space settings under Legendre-type generators.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress on Bregman analogues, indicating ongoing development rather than full resolution.

status_evidence.title: Legendre Functions Whose Gradients Map Convex Sets to Convex Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies structural conditions on Legendre generators relevant to Bregman convexity preservation.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of admissible Legendre generators is partially understood.
